title: MSDS Documentation for Interior Framing Materials
description: Learn how to organize and verify MSDS documentation for interior framing materials, match current SDS files, and separate safety, design, and shipment records.
html:
MSDS is the older term for what Canadian WHMIS now calls a Safety Data Sheet, or SDS. For interior framing materials, the useful task is not simply finding a PDF. You need to select the right document for the question, verify that it matches the material and revision, and keep safety, design, environmental, and shipment records separate.

MSDS and SDS: What the Terms Mean in Canada

MSDS and SDS refer to the same general type of safety document, but SDS is the current Canadian term. You may still see “MSDS” in older project files, supplier emails, workplace templates, and search queries.

An SDS describes the hazards associated with a hazardous product and explains safe use, handling, storage, and disposal. It contains more detailed information than a product label. Health Canada’s WHMIS supplier guidance explains the purpose of an SDS and supplier obligations.

An SDS is only one part of WHMIS communication. Ontario also requires labels and worker education, so a PDF in a project folder does not replace product labelling or worker instruction. Ontario’s WHMIS overview describes these communication elements.

Which Construction Document Answers Your Question?

The right document depends on the question. An SDS answers a workplace-safety question, while a product data sheet, load table, installation instruction, or submittal answers a technical or approval question.

DocumentUse it to answerIt does not prove
SDS, formerly MSDSWhat hazards, handling controls, storage conditions, emergency measures, and disposal information apply?Structural capacity, fire rating, acoustic rating, installation suitability, or code compliance.
Product data sheetWhat are the product’s dimensions, material, finish, profiles, and intended applications?That it satisfies every workplace condition or project-specific design.
Installation instructionsHow should the component be installed, fastened, spaced, or coordinated?That the complete assembly has a particular rating unless approved documentation says so.
Load table or engineering documentationHow do span, load, spacing, thickness, and support conditions affect selection?Hazard communication information.
HPDWhat intentionally disclosed ingredients or substances are associated with a product?A substitute for an SDS, structural evidence, or a complete environmental assessment.
EPDWhat environmental impacts are reported over a defined life-cycle scope?Workplace hazard controls or structural performance.
Submittal packageWhat combined product, design, certification, and installation information is submitted for review?That every included file applies to every product variation.

These documents work together, but they are not interchangeable. An SDS may help evaluate handling controls for a coating or accessory, while a load table supports review of stud design conditions.

Build a Documentation Register by Material and Purpose

Organize records by the material actually being received, stored, or installed, then assign each file a purpose. This prevents a general “steel framing” folder from mixing safety records with design evidence and shipment paperwork.

Steel studs, track, and channels

For steel studs, standard track, slotted deflection track, bridging channels, furring channels, and resilient channels, record the manufacturer, product family, profile, material, finish, and relevant thickness or gauge. The SDS question is whether the specific product is hazardous and requires that document. The design question may require product data, load tables, drawings, specifications, and installation details.

Keep different technical records distinct. A standard-track data sheet should not be filed as proof of the movement or installation requirements for slotted deflection track, and an SDS should not be used as design evidence.

Clips, trims, panels, and accessories

Clips, cornerbead, flat strips, panels, and other accessories may have different materials, finishes, packaging, or applied products. Record each item as it appears in the material schedule or purchase order, then identify whether the relevant record is an SDS, product data sheet, installation instruction, or another document.

Pay particular attention to paints, coatings, adhesives, sealants, or other applied substances. The safety information may relate to the applied material rather than the underlying metal component.

Separate safety, environmental, and technical records

Keep safety records separate from environmental and technical records. An EPD or HPD may support sustainability or transparency requirements, but neither replaces an SDS when workplace hazard information is required.

A practical register can use these columns: material description, manufacturer, product family, model or profile, finish, document type, revision date, file location, project requirement, and review status.

How to Verify That an SDS Is the Right One

A downloadable PDF is not automatically a suitable project record. Before filing or distributing an SDS, match it to the material that will arrive, be stored, or be used at the workplace.

  1. Confirm the manufacturer or supplier. Check the legal or trading name, address, telephone number, and emergency contact details. Compare them with the purchase order.
  2. Match the exact product identity. Record the product name, family, profile, model, catalogue number, or other identifier. A broad material description is usually not enough for document control.
  3. Check the variation. Compare coating, finish, thickness, gauge, treatment, packaging, and any included accessory.
  4. Review the revision or issue date. Record the date and document number. Preserve revision history required by your document-control process.
  5. Check completeness. Review identification, hazards, composition where applicable, first aid, firefighting, accidental release, handling, storage, exposure controls, physical properties, stability, toxicology, disposal, transport, regulatory information, and revision details as applicable.
  6. Confirm language and accessibility. Store the file where supervisors and workers can retrieve it without relying on a personal email account.
  7. Compare the project requirement. File the correct document type against the correct material instead of sending an undifferentiated folder of PDFs.

If two files show different finishes, dates, or manufacturer details, place the record on hold and resolve the discrepancy with the supplier or document owner. Do not select a version based only on its filename or download location.

Using SDS Documentation at the Warehouse and Jobsite

An SDS becomes useful when connected to a simple work process. Receiving teams, installers, supervisors, and safety coordinators may each use different parts of the same document.

During receiving

Compare the material received with the purchase order and product identity on the SDS. Look for a different coating, package, product family, or supplier. Record the accepted revision in the project register and resolve discrepancies before distribution.

During storage

Use handling and storage information to identify relevant conditions, incompatible materials, storage limits, and spill controls. Keep the SDS accessible to the people responsible for the material.

During cutting and installation

Review exposure controls, personal protective equipment, ventilation, handling, and accidental-release information where applicable. The SDS does not determine stud spacing, fasteners, deflection movement, load capacity, fire rating, or acoustic performance.

During an exposure, spill, or emergency

Use first-aid, firefighting, accidental-release, and emergency-contact information for the product involved. Do not substitute a generic metal-framing file when the event involves a coating, adhesive, sealant, or other associated product.

Ontario employers have a general duty to obtain or prepare a current SDS for hazardous products present in the workplace, and employers purchasing hazardous products must obtain supplier SDSs. Ontario’s WHMIS and employer guidance explains this responsibility.

SDS Documentation and Shipment Records Are Not the Same

An SDS communicates workplace hazards. A shipment or transport record supports movement of goods and may involve product identity, quantity, packaging, carrier requirements, route, and transport classification where applicable.

An SDS may contain transport information, but it does not automatically replace every shipping document or determine the classification of every framing product. Separate the SDS from bills of lading, carrier forms, customs records, and other shipment paperwork.

For document control, link the shipment record to the purchase order and material schedule, while linking the SDS to the product identity and revision. This gives receiving staff a way to reconcile the physical delivery without treating transport paperwork as safety or design evidence.

Control Missing and Superseded Files

When a required file is missing, record the gap in the documentation register and identify the exact material or document type involved. Do not fill the gap with a generic file from another product family or an old document whose variation cannot be confirmed.

For a replacement record, provide the manufacturer, supplier, exact product name, family, profile or model, finish, thickness or gauge where relevant, project, intended use, and required revision status. Ask the document owner to state whether the file applies to the variation ordered.

When a new revision arrives, preserve the superseded file according to the project’s document-control process, mark it as superseded, and place the current version in the active folder. If no SDS applies because the product is not classified as hazardous, record that determination separately from the product’s technical documentation.

Employers can prepare a workplace SDS in limited circumstances, but it must contain at least the required information and indicate that a supplier SDS is available. For most construction procurement workflows, obtaining the current supplier document is clearer. Federal WHMIS employer guidance describes these responsibilities.

A Project-File Checklist for MSDS and SDS Documentation

  • Material identity: manufacturer, supplier, product family, profile, model, part number, finish, and relevant thickness or gauge.
  • Document purpose: safety, product data, installation, design, environmental disclosure, or shipment.
  • Revision control: issue date, revision number, file name, date received, and superseded-file status.
  • Scope: confirm the file applies to the exact material variation.
  • Contacts: supplier and manufacturer information, including emergency details where shown.
  • Project fit: record the specification section, submittal requirement, purchase order, or reviewer request.
  • Jobsite access: store the current safety file where supervisors and workers can retrieve it.
  • Document separation: keep safety records distinct from design calculations, load tables, installation instructions, environmental documents, and shipment records.
  • Open questions: list unresolved differences in identity, finish, revision, language, or acceptance requirements.

A controlled structure might use Project / Manufacturer / Product Family / Document Type / Revision. A useful filename is Manufacturer_ProductFamily_Finish_SDS_Revision-Date.pdf.

Frequently Asked Questions About MSDS Documentation

Are MSDS and SDS the same document?

They describe the same general safety-document function, but MSDS is older terminology and SDS is the current Canadian WHMIS term. Use SDS in new records while searching both terms for legacy files.

Which document should I use for an interior framing submittal?

Use the document that answers the reviewer’s question. An SDS supports workplace hazard communication, product data supports material and profile information, installation instructions support field use, and load tables or engineering documents support design conditions. A complete submittal package may contain several of these records.

How can I tell whether an SDS is current?

Check the product identity, manufacturer details, revision or issue date, document number, applicable variation, and project acceptance requirements. Record the active version and mark older versions as superseded according to the project’s document-control process.

What is the difference between an SDS and a shipping document?

An SDS communicates workplace hazards and safe handling information. A shipping document supports transport and may contain different carrier, packaging, and classification information. An SDS does not automatically replace shipment paperwork.

Do all interior framing components use one SDS?

No single rule should be assumed from the material category alone. Review the identity, finish, coating, treatment, and classification of each product family. Keep separate records where the products or applied substances differ.

Can an SDS prove that steel framing meets structural, fire, acoustic, or code requirements?

No. Use approved product data, load tables, engineering documents, tested assembly information, installation instructions, specifications, and submittals for those decisions.
